title: release-evidence/v0 Release Evidence Bundle
description: DRAFT (v1 freezes only after the first deploy adapter runs against a real deployment; re-plan 2026-08-22). One bundle = the evidence assembled for ONE ATTEMPT of one release, SEALED AT `prepared` AND IMMUTABLE FROM THEN ON: its JCS (RFC 8785) sha256 is the bundle_digest every event of the attempt carries, so any change -- a new tree, a corrected field, a deviation discovered later -- is by definition a NEW attempt starting at prepared, never an edit (sol architect review 2026-08-22, must-3/must-4). Evidence that can only exist after sealing (a merged lane's done overlay) arrives as an `attested` event pinned to this digest, not as a bundle edit. Array order is normative for digest stability: artifacts[] sorted ascending by digest, known_deviations[] sorted ascending, no duplicates in either (collection-checked; JCS canonicalizes keys, not array order -- sol must-5). NOTE: this contract is NOT a superset of release-observation/v0; deriving an observation event from a bundle + its ledger is a defined projection documented in the protocol, with renames stated there explicitly (sol must-1 -- the earlier superset claim was wrong and is withdrawn).

release_id.description: Same identity release-observation/v0 uses (e.g. "spec-lane@0.6.0"). Attempts of one release share it; the attempt identity is (release_id, bundle_digest).

repo.description: Durable identifier (owner/name), never a local filesystem path -- same rule and incident-derived rationale as release-observation/v0's source_ref.repo.

commit_sha.description: 40 hex (SHA-1 repo) or 64 hex (SHA-256 repo) -- same dual width release-observation/v0 accepts. Within one source object, commit_sha and tree_digest MUST have the same width (bundle-level semantic check): one repository has one hash algorithm.

tree_digest.description: git tree object id of the commit's root tree. The tree, not the commit, is what the production gate compares across a squash merge (D5).

oneOf.description: Digest pins of the lane artifacts that existed AT SEAL TIME. Deliberately no done_overlay_digest: the done overlay cannot exist for a pre-merge preview, and adding it later would change the sealed digest -- it arrives as an `attested` event instead (sol must-3). The production gate for a lane-backed bundle is collection-checked: a lane_done_overlay attestation must precede deployed|production.

lane_ref.description: NULL -- not omitted -- when no lane produced this release; lane_ref_omitted is then required (and forbidden otherwise).

code.description: Closed reason codes, not free text alone: a bare string lets any release opt out of evidence by writing a sentence, and collapses 'no lane exists' with 'many lanes contributed' -- a distinction release-observation/v0 already documented as a known limit (sol must-10). A production gate can allowlist codes; it cannot allowlist prose.

review.description: PR provenance for the source that reached the default branch; head_sha comes from the GitHub API envelope, never a marker payload (D11). NULL with review_omitted for releases with no per-release review. D5's caveat stands: approve is provenance, not release-safety evidence -- the machine's verified events are the safety record. The production gate treats decision=commented as not-a-pass (collection-checked).

digest.description: package: digest of the published file (release-observation/v0's artifact_digest, projected). static_site: the content root digest -- sha256 over the canonical path->sha256 manifest (format normatively defined in the protocol; NOT a tarball digest, which embeds mtimes/ordering).

content_manifest_digest.description: static_site only (required there, forbidden elsewhere -- both schema-enforced): sha256 over the BYTES of the release-manifest.json file actually placed into the deployed site and read back after deploy. That file is {schema_version, content} ONLY -- it deliberately does NOT embed bundle_digest, because the bundle embeds THIS digest: a file that also embedded the bundle's digest would make the two mutually referential and neither computable (found by the first real adapter assembly, 2026-08-22). The site<->bundle linkage is re-derived at read-back instead: JCS-sha256 of the file's content map must equal this artifact's `digest`.

distribution.description: Required for pypi (schema-enforced): one PyPI release publishes wheel+sdist with different sha256 each -- release-observation/v0 measured this live; without naming the file the digest resolves to nothing.

verifiability.description: Measured per registry, not asserted: release-observation/v0 confirmed live that PyPI metadata exposes sha256 (registry_metadata) and npm exposes only sha1/sha512 (requires_fetch). npm + registry_metadata is therefore schema-rejected.

artifacts.description: Sorted ascending by digest, digests unique (collection/bundle semantic check -- array order is inside the JCS digest, so order must be deterministic; sol must-5).

known_deviations.description: Deviations KNOWN AT SEAL TIME only (sol must-4): anything discovered later must not edit the sealed bundle -- it belongs in an append-only record pinned to this bundle's digest (v0 defines no such record yet; v1 will, informed by the first real case). Sorted ascending, unique (semantic check).

previous_release_id.description: The release to return to if this one is rolled back; must differ from this bundle's own release_id (semantic check) and, when a ledger is checked alongside, must resolve within it. NULL only for a first-ever release of a target.
